title: Her rooms on B deck (the bridge deck): R3, a sourced table of facts
written: 2026-11-20, by the R3 session (Claude Opus 5.5), under docs/research/RESEARCH_rooms_plans_licence_v1_1_2026-11-20.md, on the coordinator's word after D deck and the orlop
rules: Facts only: which room, where, how big, which door to which. No image or drawing of any plan is kept. Every row cites the reference read and the original checked, or says it was not checked. Bets are tagged as bets.
reference: ET: Encyclopedia Titanica's free deck plans, B deck (https://www.encyclopedia-titanica.org/titanic-deckplans/b-deck.html; drawn by Bruce Beveridge for Titanic The Ship Magnificent, The History Press 2008), read on the page in the built-in browser on 2026-11-20, nothing saved
original: Shipbuilder 1911: The Shipbuilder, Midsummer 1911 (the Olympic and Titanic number), its plate of the bridge deck (B), as reproduced by GG Archives (https://www.ggarchives.com/OT/Titanic/25-ImageLibrary/TheShipbuilder-10-Design-SpecialPlates.html); too small to read room by room, not opened this time.
how: Walls by her frames, as on C deck: the plan's scale from its own frame ticks (30.85 px a frame amidships: 0.0975 ft a pixel), the midship section between the ticks of 1A and 1F (by the printed 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 aft of it), a ruler of her frames drawn over the page at that scale; the plan's printed frames at 140A and 140F fall on it within a few inches. Walls read against the ruler at 1:2 (to about a frame) and 1:1; the house's sides, the passages and the house's front by pixel profiles at 1:1 (rows tagged 'profiled').

Frames to feet: E deck's anchors (data/rooms/E_deck.json). The rows run from the house's after end to its front; the forecastle and the poop on B deck are weather decks with no rooms (capstans, cranes, hatches, the docking bridge over the poop).

y: feet from the centreline, port positive, at 0.0979 ft a pixel (945 px between her sides amidships). 'shell+' and 'shell-' are her side; in metres the tool puts it at the model's half-breadth halfway between B and A decks [stand-in for the reference's shell].
Block level: a row is a block of rooms between passages (cabin numbers in plan), a public room, a casing, a stair or a service block.
No watertight bulkhead reaches B deck; the table's bulkheads is empty.

Doors: 2 ft 3 in by default [bet], unless the reference writes one: the doors in her side on the second-class promenade (a folding-down gangway door 10 ft 0 in clear; passenger doors of 4 ft 9 in and 4 ft 0 in) and the 4 ft 6 in doors at the house's front. Stairs are listed among the doors with no width.
Derived fields (x_m, y_m, poly_m, area_m2, zone, slab, plan_compartment) are written by: node tools/rooms_table.js --write data/rooms/B_deck.json

frames.note: E deck's anchors (her frames, feet forward of amidships).

bulkheads.note: None: no watertight bulkhead reaches B deck, and the reference marks none.

side.note: Read 2026-11-21 between 05:20 and 05:45 CST by the B1+B2 lane with R3's method and line test, both sides, in the built-in browser (nothing saved), from 80A to 80F only, for C3 (the epoch's hull ends, D80; G20's G14 half): it removes R3's bet of C deck's side for the C-to-B band there. B deck's ends (the poop, the forecastle) are not read. Every 5 frames, no reading off the smooth line through its neighbours by more than 0.1 m. For BACKLOG G14 (the hull's ends): tools/rooms_table_tests.js sets each against the model's half-breadth.
side.unit: ft from the centreline to her outer line as the plan draws it, port and starboard, read on the page at 1:1 by pixel profile: from her outside inward, the first dark pixel that lies on a continuous line (a dark path running at least 28 px each way along her), at three columns 6 px apart about the frame's tick; the median of the three. Annotations outside her (labels, dimension arrows) fail the line test. null: no reading (the line broken there by fittings).
